statement: The function returns a result r and, for every byte vector t, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = t is 1 if t is a valid sentence and is 0 otherwise. A byte vector t is a valid sentence exactly when there exist an integer k >= 1 and indices j_0,...,j_{k-1} with 0 <= j_l < len(wordDict) for every l, such that s equals the byte concatenation of wordDict[j_0], wordDict[j_1], ..., wordDict[j_{k-1}] in that order, and t equals the byte concatenation of wordDict[j_0], then one byte 32 (ASCII space), then wordDict[j_1], then one byte 32, ..., then one byte 32, then wordDict[j_{k-1}]. In particular, r contains every valid sentence exactly once, in any order, and contains no other vectors.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 20; 1 <= len(wordDict) <= 1000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(wordDict), 1 <= len(wordDict[j]) <= 10; every byte of s and of every wordDict[j] is an ASCII lowercase letter (97 <= byte <= 122); for all j and k with 0 <= j < k < len(wordDict), wordDict[j] != wordDict[k].
